messages:
Liam O'Connor: Quick heads-up : procurement is updating the provisional PO rules today. New memo below.

Sofia Patel: Thanks Liam. What changed?

Liam O'Connor: TL;DR: provisional POs can be issued for existing vetted vendors up to $7,500 (was $5k). Anything above requires a signed contract. Provisional POs must include `expires_at` and `procurement_owner`.

Procurement Bot: Automated note: provisional PO template updated in Supplier Portal -> Templates. Fields required: vendor_id, amount, expires_at (ISO), procurement_owner, provisional=true.

Sofia Patel: Does this affect virtual cards and recurring SaaS renewals?

Liam O'Connor: No change for recurring SaaS — renewals still follow the renewal workflow. Virtual card one-off trial charges should still use the `virtual-card` request and obey vendor limits.

Legal Review: To add: provisional POs >$2k will trigger a parallel legal review flag so we can catch T&Cs. This won't block creating the provisional PO but will stop invoice payment until legal disposition.

Sofia Patel: Noted. Can we get an announcement copy for our managers so they know to attach receipts within 7 days? We've seen late uploads causing reconciliation friction.

Liam O'Connor: Sure : short announcement for managers: "Receipts must be uploaded within 7 days of charge. Provisional POs expire automatically; do not rely on them for long-term commitments. For exceptions, open a vendor-exception ticket." I'll post to #finance later today.

Procurement Bot: Reminder: any provisional PO marked `provisional=true` will auto-expire at `expires_at`. After expiration, vendor invoices will be rejected unless converted to a standard PO.

Sofia Patel: Great. I'll circulate to the vendor ops channel and update the PO checklist.

Liam O'Connor: Thanks. If anyone needs a 1:1 on converting provisional POs to contracts, ping me.
